11 September, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.38960 of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate Writ or direction declaring the action of the respondents in not acquiring the land and structures of residents of Nagardoddi village (B.C Colony), Dharoor Mandal as illegal and arbitrary and consequently direct the respondents to acquire the land and structures pay compensation and provide rehabilitation to the Villagers of Nagardoddi village (B.C Colony), Dharoor Mandal as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparence in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ..."
2.

sentences.text: It is stated that the petitioners are the residents of Nagardoddi Village (B.C Colony), Dharoor Mandal, Mahabubnagar District.

It is their case that the Government vide G.O.Ms.No.278 Irrigation & CAD (Irrigation-V) Department dated 26.10.1995 has issued orders for acquisition of land and structures of their village and five other villages i.e., Uppair, Garlaparu, Anugonda, Ankampally and Dadanpally, as they were under submergence of the Priyadarshini Jurala Project and in terms of the said G.O, a committee, which was constituted for the purpose of inspection, has submitted a report recommending acquisition of houses of the above villages.

It is the further case of the petitioners that respondent No.2 has issued notification, dated 21.08.2013, under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act No.1/1894 proposing to acquire the houses of their Village and thereafter,

respondent No.1 published the declaration under Section 6 of the Act for acquisition of lands in Sy.Nos.93/2, 94/2, 95/2 and 96/2 of Nagardoddi Village for rehabilitating the displaced persons of the their village and appointed respondent No.3 as Land Acquisition Officer (LAO).

The grievance of the petitioners is that the respondents have passed award, paid compensation and provided alternative lands under rehabilitation and resettlement scheme to all the displaced persons of the above five villages, but have neither passed the award nor paid the compensation to their village,
within the stipulated time and there are no land acquisition proceedings in respect of their lands till date.
3.

This writ petition is pending on the file of this Court from 2015 and the respondents have not filed any counter affidavit and there is no dispute with regard to issuance of notification under Section 4(1) of the Act followed by declaration under Section 6 of the Act.

4. sentences.text: 1 under the submergence of Priyadarshini Jurala Project, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of this writ petition directing the respondents to consider the case of the petitioners in terms of the said G.O, if the houses of the petitioners are falling under the said Project and take appropriate steps in accordance with law, within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
5. With the above directions, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
